title: See the energy.

intro: A site’s energy story goes beyond its electricity bill. From live monitoring and demand management to storage dispatch, EMS is designed around a complete management cycle, with site data behind each decision.
sceneLabel: From equipment to the whole site
story: Equipment starts up and demand rises. At peak time, the team needs to know: what changed, does demand need attention, and could storage help?
When readings, alarms and reports live in different places, each question takes several searches. EMS brings observation, interpretation, management and review into one connected workflow.
steps: Start with the site and its equipment. Review current readings, status and alarms to find changes that need attention.
Compare trends, demand and equipment records. Establish when and under what conditions a change occurred before discussing a strategy.
Bring storage dispatch, event tracking and reporting into one cycle, reviewing how each strategy relates to site operation.
capabilitiesIntro: Six connected areas define the intended EMS scope. The demo supports workflow discussions; data connections, control conditions and delivery scope are confirmed for each site.
capabilities: Move from a site overview to equipment readings through a shared starting point for daily checks.
Place a change on a timeline and compare operating periods with original records to understand its context.
Consider peaks, demand trends and site objectives together to inform management strategies.
Review storage status, charging needs and site use together to establish workable dispatch conditions.
Follow an event from detection through the underlying records to its handling and review.
Organize operating and management records for a period so different teams can discuss the same evidence.

stages: Does today’s energy use look familiar?
